title: Nebula Sh2-239
caption: The star-forming nebula Sh2-239, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Bright red knots and jets stand out in this view of Sh2-239, especially inside a cavity at the top center of the image. Sh2-239 is a distinct nebula in the constellation Taurus where stars have been forming for quite a long time.
It holds two clusters of very young stars that are still deeply embedded in the cloud, along with many older, more evolved stars.

Those red knots and jets are outflows. Young stars often blast narrow jets of gas away from their poles as they grow, and where the jets slam into the surrounding cloud, the gas lights up. Seeing so many outflows here is a sign of an active nursery, with stars at different stages of development sharing the same neighborhood.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope used four filters. B is shown in blue, V in green, I in orange and hydrogen-alpha in red.
